line: Misaeng: not yet alive. A group on a go board that is neither alive nor dead.
It started with his uncle's stones. He nearly swallowed a few. It didn't spoil the fun.
Go on, then. Where would you play?
beats.speaker: un

line: Baduk is good for concentration, his uncle said, and his mother gladly paid for the neighbourhood class. Soon he was winning his uncle's and his father's bets back from Mr. Kim at the laundromat.
Then an amateur six-dan's academy. His mother objected; nobody thought he'd conquer the baduk world. Nobody could stop a nine-year-old with a problem book at dawn, either.
Then a professional's dojang. Prodigy: to his parents the word was a sedative. And his father's company had just gone under.

args: At eleven he entered the Korea Baduk Association as a trainee. He is eighteen now.

line: At home his parents cut Lee Chang-ho and Lee Sedol out of the papers: rankings, prize money.
Only now does he see his father's wrinkles, and how dull his mother's eyes have gone.
The day he leaves is an ordinary day. Tomorrow, it feels, he'll be back here, losing to younger kids. He hasn't changed. Everyone else has, and the colour has gone out of the world.
Not talent. Not luck, or the half-point losses. Not the part-time jobs, or his father's death, or his mother in bed. Those would hurt too much. So: he didn't try hard enough.
He walks away dropping stones from his pocket, a few at a time.
Because he didn't try hard enough, he had to come out into the world. Because he didn't try hard enough, he was thrown away.
Kang Ho-ryong and Ahn Sang-gi, his friends from the trainee room, turned pro last year.
You're really quitting? After everything you've put in?
beats.speaker: hy

line: He has no answer. At home he ties up his game records, and puts them out with the board.
The restaurant failed. His mother worked building sites until her body gave out. He studied for the equivalency exam between part-time jobs, and in the bathroom he washed her back.
His sponsor gave him a job at his company. Baduk? What dan? Then: why did you quit? Then: no flexibility. He fled to the army.
Go and thank him. The president who gave you that job. You owe him that.
beats.speaker: mo

line: I've talked to a friend who runs a trading company. Only he knows about the baduk. It'll be a simple interview.
beats.speaker: sp

line: But your papers are thin. You'll go in with nothing. Some will call you a parachute.
beats.speaker: sp

line: The city puts its make-up on: toasting, flattering, going home. Start from the bottom, like everyone else. Don't fail the way you failed at baduk.
If there's a light I must keep burning, I'll answer for it. If there's a light allowed me. Is there one, for me?

args: The alarm. The alarm again. A struggling group from the very first move.

line: A message from upstairs: don't come to the office. Go straight to a café in Jongno. A buyer is waiting, and nobody else can meet him.
Oh Sang-sik, section head, Sales Team 3. Red eyes, stubble, three sons. He promised them the mountain, on a Wednesday.
He forgot the eleven o'clock meeting with an overseas buyer. On the summit, his phone rings.
Where are you? The buyer's waiting. If he walks, we both die.
beats.speaker: ms_bujang

line: Anyone can go, sir. The director. The executives. The president himself.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: I'm sending today's new hire straight there. Are we in a position to be picky?
beats.speaker: ms_bujang

line: A rookie? On his first day?
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Into the car. The road in moves five hundred metres in thirty minutes.
There was a paper at the workshop. Fear is mostly irrational...
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Shall I tell you about dismissal-notice pay?
beats.speaker: ms_bujang

line: Mangwon-dong crossroads. Twelve kilometres an hour. Eight to go. Thirty minutes late. Fear is rational.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: A buyer from overseas and his manager, Kang. From One International, only a new hire with no papers. He can't talk trade. He can talk one thing.
A puzzle? All right. Black to play?
beats.speaker: by

line: Play inside. Let them take it. Take back more.
Oh bursts in, thirty minutes late, hiking clothes under his jacket.
Your young man kept us busy. The quiz was fun.
beats.speaker: ks

line: No. I found it on the internet.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Oh's car: a battered laptop, paper cups, red eyes on the road.
Kim. The Malaysian claim: it's FOB, the damage is in the packing, that's the carrier's. Push back.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Jang understands none of it. But he once lost to a trainee just like this: sloppy, red-eyed, bored. He read him as careless, and was wrong.
Obsessive. Responsible. A man who carries everything.
Oh nods at the wheel, and washes down a handful of vitamins.
Jang Geu-rae is an intern, with Sales Team 3. In two months there's a PT test.
beats.speaker: hr

line: I'm your mentor. Kim Dong-sik is your buddy.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Assistant manager Kim. First: this requisition, to General Affairs.
beats.speaker: kd

line: An executive's words come back to him: a special case. No university, no specialty. Build one before the PT.
General Affairs hands over a box of supplies, a glue stick among them.
Sort these files into my folders.
beats.speaker: kd

line: He draws a mind map and builds a better tree. It takes an afternoon.
Where are my folders? Who do you think you are?
beats.speaker: kd

line: That structure is the company's. This isn't work you do alone. It's work you do together.
beats.speaker: kd

line: At fifteen he filed his game records his own way. A system only he ever had to read.
Interns' study tonight. And we find out who the dud is.
beats.speaker: gl

line: A bar full of interns pitching PT topics. Ahn Young-yi, the only woman among them, watches him.
You haven't said a word. You won't learn by listening.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: And you've got filing due tomorrow, and you're sitting here? Secure your own stones, then attack.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: He lived by that proverb all his life, and had to hear it from someone else. He runs back to the office.
He really does have filing due. Come on. You're going to apologise.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Sorry. I didn't know you had urgent work.
beats.speaker: gl

line: His scheme is rational. But only the staff share the old order.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: Keep Kim's order for the executives' file. Use Jang's cross-index from the planning stage, and departments could line up.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: She kept herself alive, and him too. Both live.
That night he dreams of a board: rows of white stones, and one black.
Up before the alarm, crushed on the train. Am I the only one still dreaming? The world is faster than me.
A ten-day claim window, missed! Ten days! ...I'm going to the sauna.
beats.speaker: am

line: Plain and safe, not perfect and late.
Kim's B/L call to the forwarder. The copies. The floor. All at once.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: The PT dates are set: the first week of next month, a whole week at the training centre. Individual tasks and a team task. Think about partners.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Everyone wants you. No confidence, no skills. Pair with a sure dud and you shine.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Be careful of whoever comes to you first.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Whoever your partner is, trust them. The one inside the board can't see his own scheming. Everyone watching can.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Do your part, and trust the rest.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Han Seok-yul. I came back from the Ulsan plant for the PT.
beats.speaker: han

line: Sente: leading the game. He has always handed it over. This time he leads.
Mechanical engineering. Contest prizes. Plant tours, foreign buyers, a meal with the president. Stone after stone, slammed down in handfuls.
Team up with me. Build the PT however you like. Mail me your progress.
beats.speaker: han

line: They say he made a big mistake in front of a buyer at Ulsan.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: A total dud. Who's going to be the bomb squad?
beats.speaker: gl

line: Next to the board where you fight alone, the world seems kinder, and warmer. He mails Han three PT items.
Who knows. Maybe a big dud. A nuclear bomb.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: You said I could build it my way.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: I said share it. I never said I'd keep my mouth shut.
beats.speaker: ms_han

line: In the next stall, the glasses intern heard every word.
You begged, so you got one more chance. If you're not sure of yourself, go back to a desk.
beats.speaker: ul

line: Night, in Seoul. Stones spilled by an abandoned board, and Jang at his screen. The world is far colder, and more heartless.
You call this a plan? An after-school hobby? Where I interned, one item took four days.
beats.speaker: ms_han

line: Please check it. If it's short, I'll redo it.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: That night: forty-two pages. Forty. Fifty-three.
Colours that don't match, boxes all over the place. What did you do yesterday?
beats.speaker: oh

line: The interns had the PT exam, sir.
beats.speaker: kim

line: Kim, under his breath: answer that fast and he only gets angrier.
He slips into an empty meeting room and calls Ulsan.
Baduk is a war with a plain winner and loser, and he lived in it for over ten years. A beaten soldier, but raised to compete. A player who doesn't hand over sente.
Then we chose it together. From here I write the PT my way. I'll share the progress, but I don't take instructions.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: And how old are you, anyway?
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: After many short nights, he sleeps deeply at last, slumped in a chair in an empty meeting room.
His partner's Han Seok-yul. Han's a talker. I'd bet Jang's doing all the work.
beats.speaker: kd

line: A smooth talker, and one who can't tell he's being used. Some team.
beats.speaker: oh

line: He dreams of his heroes. Cho Nam-chul, Cho Hunhyun, Lee Chang-ho, Lee Sedol. One by one they fade. Haven't I let go of baduk yet?
You were crying in your sleep. Your partner's Han? He'll use anyone to shine.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: An ambitious man is a tornado. But the eye of a tornado is calm. Get into his centre, and you two could really work.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: You've got an unusual eye, you know. Shame insight doesn't count as a specialty.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Wait, that's why I came! The seniors have called all the interns out. It's evening. You slept the whole day.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Here to sleep, or to work? He's late. Three penalty glasses.
The ones who use him, help him, get angry with him and scold him: all of them are on his side. Here, he is not an outsider.
With that, he ends today's baduk. Where the white stone fell from the board, there's a black one.
Anything with figures goes in the shredder. No paper of ours is ever found outside this team.
beats.speaker: kd

line: He'll shred the waybill later, with the next batch. It stays on his desk: Sales Team 3, DH-14.
Can I borrow your glue? Our cabinet's locked, and nobody gives me the key.
beats.speaker: sh

line: Kim Seok-ho, an intern on another team, glues his report flat at Jang's desk, the waybill underneath, and runs.
Jang feeds the shredder, humming. Down in the lobby, the yellow sheet slides off the security desk onto the floor. A director taps it with his shoe.
Director! Is this about a team dinner?
beats.speaker: oh

line: Without a word, the director kicks the team's paper box over. His aide hands Oh the waybill: found on the lobby floor.
On the roof, the interns are yelled at. At his desk, Oh turns the waybill over. Glued to it: a torn scrap of a weekly report. Kim Seok-ho.
Applause from across the floor. Go, a section head on Sales Team 1, comes over pumping his fists.
My baby intern, Kim Seok-ho! All-nighters with us, newly married, eldest son of an eldest son. And we've just landed it.
beats.speaker: go

line: He comes to our team a lot. To borrow supplies.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Ha! My fault. The supply cabinet's key is on my key ring.
beats.speaker: go

line: Oh looks at the waybill in his hands. A locked cabinet. A borrowed glue stick. A scrap with a name on it.
Jang told everyone the waybill was his fault. Oh took him and Kim for a drink. It isn't nine yet, and Oh is already tipsy.
Geu-rae did nothing wrong today. It's bad to be misunderstood.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Jealous, Oh? You snub my intern over a few supplies, and now you want to spoil our win?
beats.speaker: go

line: Get your intern his own glue! Mine took the blame because yours got glue on a document and dropped it!
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Go doesn't take it in. Kim Seok-ho does.
Late, Kim Seok-ho comes home to one room. The baby is awake, and knows him. Her hand closes round his finger.
In another room, in the dark, Jang sets stones on a board, one at a time.
Not yet. The scrap, the glue, the key. Put it together first.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Incheon harbour at first light: cargo meant for Gunsan, unloaded here, some of it damaged. He went to see it himself. Paper drifts from the site.
Back on the thirteenth floor: Steve Han, head of the Americas textile team, has come to pick a fight with Kim Bu-ryeon, head of Sales 1 to 3. Same rank. Everyone is watching.
I don't have time for a report this thick. A fat report is how nobody takes responsibility.
beats.speaker: st

line: My team was up all night on it.
beats.speaker: br

line: I need to understand the client, not your catalogue. Who's it for? What climate? What taste? Just tell me what I need.
beats.speaker: st

line: Everyone plays their own baduk. Whoever prepared better is happier with the result. Whoever rushed to keep pace has no excuse.
Why would Steve come down on our department head? Out with it.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Steve suggested a dinner with the buyers. I picked the place. I'd had a few.
beats.speaker: go

line: Go had taken a buyer, and Steve, to a dog-meat restaurant, read Steve wrong, and never said sorry. Steve sat on Sales Team 1's approvals.
And our department head is too sore to apologise. In a way, it's checkmate.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Baduk words, from people who don't play. Jang grins.
You're laughing while your seniors talk?
beats.speaker: kd

line: Apologising is the only way. In baduk you don't leave dead stones on the board. A dead stone left lying there grows into a bigger problem.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Easier said. He's proud. An office runs on politics.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Then let's do politics with class. Being humble when it counts: that's class. Let's go.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Kim Bu-ryeon isn't at his desk. He left scowling, someone says, with Go.
Behind a partition on the textile floor: Kim Bu-ryeon is already there, with Go.
I didn't know what had happened. I'm sorry.
beats.speaker: br

line: And I'm sorry I lost my temper. Thank you for coming yourself.
beats.speaker: st

line: I'm sorry. ...So will the approvals go faster now?
beats.speaker: go

line: Often the obvious move is the hardest. Some things you must do however hard, and some you must not do however easy.
